title: A Preregistered Paired Evaluation of Generate–Verify–Repair (GVR) for Intent→Configuration NetOps: Null Results on a Synthetic Verifier-Checked Task Bank
abstract: We report a fully preregistered, archived paired experiment testing whether a deterministic verifier plus a bounded LLM-guided repair loop (Generate–Verify–Repair, GVR) reduces verifier-detected semantic invariant violations for intent→device-configuration translation. The confirmatory design used a public synthetic NetOps task bank (N = 240 paired tasks), gpt-5-mini as generator (execution/model_configuration.json SHA-256: a40e96e2...), and a pybatfish-style deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5). Execution used shared-initial-candidate semantics (one generated candidate per task reused across arms), with at most one bounded repair attempt per task. All planned episodes completed (planned_episode_count = 480; completed_episode_count = 480) with model_calls_used = 240 (shared-generation). Every generated candidate satisfied the deterministic verifier in both arms: n11 = 240, n10 = n01 = n00 = 0. The paired estimate (rate_GVR − rate_baseline) = 0.0; exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.00; paired-bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0] (10,000 resamples; bootstrap_seed = 1729). Two preregistration/execution deviations materially constrain inference and are explicitly disclosed: (1) the executed shared-generation semantics invalidated the preregistered power calculation that assumed independent per-condition generation, and (2) a prespecified comparison (GVR vs schema-constrained baseline, C vs B) was not executed and no recorded rationale appears in the archive. Conservatively interpreted, bounded GVR provided no verifier-detectable benefit in this specific artifact-grounded setting because there were no verifier-detectable errors to correct. We release and analyze the archival artifacts and recommend reproducible next steps (independent per-condition generation, adversarial/golden injections, multi-model runs, and broader verifier coverage).

sections.introduction: LLM-driven intent→configuration translation offers operational efficiency for network operations (NetOps) but risks generating syntactically plausible yet semantically harmful configuration changes that violate reachability, workflow, or policy invariants. Prior work therefore recommends architectures that interpose deterministic validators and iterative repair (generate–verify–repair, GVR) to detect and correct mechanically checkable defects before committing changes. We conducted a fully preregistered, archived paired experiment to test a focused operational question: under a frozen design that used one generator/prompt pairing and shared-initial-candidate generation semantics, does inserting a deterministic verifier plus a bounded LLM-guided repair loop reduce verifier-detected semantic invariant violations relative to an unconstrained baseline? We (a) preregistered the study (preregistration_sha256: eaedeae9aa302327e090d519a7a16f514d7fb79a472071aaf171f2f618c8ad4d), (b) froze the analysis executor (paired_binary_analysis_v1), and (c) executed the run and archived all artifacts. Below we present the design, artifact-backed results, a concise evidence-to-claim mapping, required preregistration→execution deviations, statistical interpretation, and operational recommendations.
sections.related_work: Three literatures motivated the study. (1) LLM failures: surveys and empirical studies document hallucinations, fabricated code/tool calls, and generated artifacts that can be unsafe if directly executed—motivating verifier interposition [evidence_synthesis C1]. (2) Generate–verify–repair and constraint-based decoding methods: prior work shows these architectures improve mechanically checkable properties (e.g., syntactic validity, compilation) and reduce surface-level hallucinations, though domain-level semantic guarantees remain open [evidence_synthesis C2,C3]. (3) NetOps verifier and intent-translation research: intent-based systems and pybatfish-style verifiers are standard approaches to capture network invariants; human-in-the-loop workflows are recommended for high-stakes changes [evidence_synthesis C4,C5]. Our run differs by being preregistered, paired, and artifact-archived, emphasizing inferential rigor and reproducible accounting rather than broad leaderboard comparisons.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimands: The preregistered study_id is c1_gvr_semantic_eval_prereg_v1. Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline (paired difference in verifier-detected violation rates). Two primary comparisons were prespecified: (C vs A) GVR vs unconstrained generation and (C vs B) GVR vs schema-constrained decoding; Bonferroni correction across the two comparisons (family alpha = 0.05 → per-comparison alpha = 0.025). The analysis executor 'paired_binary_analysis_v1' and the sampling plan (N=240 paired tasks; 12 clusters × 20 tasks) were frozen prior to execution.

Execution contract and concrete settings (archived): adapter_family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1; requested generator = gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json SHA-256: a40e96e2...); deterministic verifier = deterministic_netops_validator_v5; task generator = deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5. Planned episodes: 480 (two scored conditions per task). Generation semantics actually executed: shared_initial_candidate (generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate; independent_condition_generation = false), meaning a single initial candidate was generated per task and reused for both arms; initial_generation_calls_per_task = 1; maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1 (bounded single repair attempt). The execution manifest documents planned_episode_count = 480, completed_episode_count = 480, failed_episode_count = 0, and model_calls_used = 240 (shared-generation audit).

Task bank and oracle: We used a public synthetic NetOps task bank (N=240 paired tasks); each task includes initial device state, intent, required workflow constraints, and expected final state. The deterministic validator implements pybatfish-style checks and returns structured diagnostics (violation_count, violations list, parsed_command_count, required_command_count). Scoring rule: full_intent_constraint_validation as implemented by deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator_version 5.0). Representative per-task traces and scoring JSON are archived under execution/scoring/ and execution/responses/ with validator traces and scores.
sections.results:
Execution accounting (artifact-backed): All planned episodes completed (planned_episode_count = 480; completed_episode_count = 480; failed_episode_count = 0). Because shared_initial_candidate semantics were executed, the run used model_calls_used = 240: one shared generation per task reused across both arms (provider-call audit and deterministic_reconciliation.json confirm this). Representative scoring artifacts (execution/scoring/task-000001-*.json) show identical shared-initial, baseline, and guarded responses for sample tasks.

Primary confirmatory outcome: Every generated candidate satisfied the deterministic verifier in both arms. The contingency table is n11 = 240 (both accepted), n10 = 0 (guarded-only), n01 = 0 (baseline-only), n00 = 0 (both rejected). Observed rates: baseline_success_rate = 1.0; guarded_success_rate = 1.0; paired estimate (rate_GVR − rate_baseline) = 0.0. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.00. Paired-bootstrap 95% CI (paired_bootstrap_percentile; bootstrap_resamples = 10000; bootstrap_seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.0]. Analysis artifacts (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, analysis/condition_summary.csv, analysis/analysis_log.jsonl) and analysis/results.json are archived and authoritative for these numbers.

Repair usage: For every episode, validator trace records repair_applied = false; the bounded repair loop was never invoked because the shared initial candidate already passed the verifier for every task. Missingness and contamination summaries report zero flags and zero failed episodes (analysis/missingness_summary.csv; analysis/contamination_summary.csv).
sections.discussion:
Statistical interpretation and degeneracy: The observed contingency (zero discordant pairs) makes the paired inference degenerate: with n10 = n01 = 0, no within-pair disagreements exist to estimate a differential effect. The exact McNemar p = 1.00 and the collapsed bootstrap CI [0.0, 0.0] are deterministic consequences of the observed contingency and the frozen analysis executor. Crucially, the preregistered power calculation assumed independent per-condition generation (which would allow stochastic discordance); the executed shared-generation semantics removed that discordance potential and thus invalidated the preregistered power argument for the run as executed. This mismatch is an explicit preregistration→execution deviation and directly explains the degenerate null outcome in the archived artifacts.

Prespecified-but-unexecuted comparison: The preregistration listed two prespecified primary comparisons (C vs A and C vs B). The archived execution artifacts document only the adapter-configured paired experiment comparing the unconstrained baseline (A) to guarded GVR (C) under shared_initial_candidate semantics. The prespecified schema-constrained-baseline comparison (C vs B) was not executed; the execution archive contains no recorded rationale for that omission. We therefore explicitly label this prespecified comparison as unexecuted and unresolved in the archival record. This procedural omission further constrains inferential breadth.

Conservative operational conclusion: Artifact-grounded and conservatively interpreted, bounded GVR (one repair attempt) provided no additional verifier-detectable benefit for this synthetic workload and the executed semantics because there were no verifier-detectable errors to correct. This null result does not imply that GVR is generally ineffective: it shows that measurable benefit depends on (a) generation semantics (shared vs independent per-arm generation), (b) generator+prompt pairing and task distribution, and (c) verifier sensitivity and coverage. Our artifacts identify these mechanisms and permit deterministic reruns under alternative semantics.

Recommendations grounded in archive: (1) Re-execute the preregistered paired design with independent per-condition generation (set independent_condition_generation = true) to restore discordance potential; the archived task manifest and RNG seeds permit deterministic reruns. (2) Inject adversarial or golden-reference tasks (the preregistration planned 10% golden tasks) whose expected verifier outcomes are known to validate verifier sensitivity. (3) Expand generator scope beyond gpt-5-mini and allow larger or iterative repair budgets to assess repair efficacy distributions. (4) Broaden verifier predicates (or integrate formal/SMT verifiers) to reduce oracle incompleteness; evidence_synthesis identifies stronger formal integration (G2) as an open gap. (5) Report both shared- and independent-generation semantics in future evaluations to clarify inferential targets.
sections.conclusion: We executed a fully preregistered, archived paired experiment of a bounded GVR intervention on a synthetic intent→configuration NetOps task bank. Under the executed shared-initial-candidate semantics (one generation per task reused across arms), every generated candidate satisfied the deterministic verifier in both arms (n11 = 240), producing a degenerate null paired estimate = 0.0, exact McNemar p = 1.00, and paired-bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0] (10,000 resamples; seed 1729). Two preregistration→execution deviations constrain inference: (1) shared-generation semantics invalidated the preregistered independent-generation power assumption, and (2) a prespecified schema-constrained-baseline comparison (C vs B) was not executed and lacks a recorded rationale in the archive. We therefore limit conclusions to the executed artifact-backed semantics: bounded GVR added no verifier-detectable value in this specific setting because there were no verifier-detectable errors to correct. All execution and analysis artifacts are archived; we encourage deterministic reruns under independent-generation, adversarial injections, multi-model configurations, and expanded verifier coverage to robustly assess GVR’s operational value for NetOps.

limitations: Synthetic task bank and verifier scope: N = 240 tasks were synthetic and evaluated against a pybatfish-style deterministic validator; results may not generalize to production topologies, vendor-specific syntax, or semantic invariants not encoded in the verifier.

Shared-generation semantics: the archived run used generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (one initial generation per task reused across arms). This design reduced model-call cost but also removed per-arm stochastic variation and therefore reduced sensitivity to detect GVR benefits that rely on independent per-condition generator variability; the preregistered power calculation assumed independent per-condition generation and therefore does not apply to the executed design.
Single-model evaluation: the experiment used one generator (gpt-5-mini); cross-model generality is not established.
Repair budget: only a single bounded repair iteration was permitted; different or larger repair budgets or iterative strategies might produce different outcomes.
Verifier completeness risk: passing the deterministic verifier does not guarantee absence of all operational risks (unobserved invariants or properties outside the verifier model).

Prespecified comparison not executed: the preregistration included a prespecified schema-constrained-baseline comparison (C vs B) that was not executed in the archived run; the artifacts do not record a rationale, which is an unresolved procedural limitation.
